title: A bundle's committed .lore/schemas/*.json can silently drift from what the active profile's generator currently produces, and lore check exits 0 on it
description:
Raised by opum-agent 2026-09-18 as a hypothesis while reconciling a false premise in an earlier
relay (see LCLI-537/538's history); independently confirmed here against lore-cli's OWN bundle,
not taken on their word -- they explicitly declined to read this repo's tree themselves and asked
me to check it, which I did.

THE DEFECT, reproduced against dev at HEAD (1bfd825d):

  bun run src/cli.ts schema export --out .repro-scratch/x   # regenerates from the active profile
  diff -rq .lore/schemas/ .repro-scratch/x/                  # all seven files differ

Committed `.lore/schemas/story.schema.json` was missing four properties the generator emits
today: `relations`, `claim_outcome`, `claim_evidence_level`, `claim_version`. Traced to commit
01f4ef74 (LCLI-477, PR #76, "typed authored relationships, and claim state as its own axis") --
the generator has produced these fields since that PR merged; `.lore/schemas/` was never
re-exported afterward. Meanwhile `lore check` on the stale, as-committed bundle: "80 files, 0
errors, 0 warnings" -- clean. Nothing in `lore check`, `lore validate`, or anywhere else compares
a committed schema file's bytes against what `schema export` would produce right now.

WHY THIS IS THE SAME FAILS-GREEN SHAPE AS LCLI-534/537/538, and arguably worse: the artifact is
version-controlled and looks authoritative. An agent (or a human, or an editor's YAML language
server via the `$schema` modeline `lore new`/`lore init` stamp) reading `.lore/schemas/story.schema.json`
to learn what a Story may contain gets a confident, wrong answer, with no warning anywhere in the
tool. This is exactly the mechanism that produced the false premise in the relay that surfaced
this: a sibling repo's stale committed schema was read as if it were current and became a claim
about lore's design.

IMMEDIATE HYGIENE FIX, done in this same change (not a fix for the general gate below): lore-cli's
own `.lore/schemas/*.json` re-exported via `lore schema export` and committed, so this repo's own
bundle stops being an instance of the problem it's filing. That does not close this task --
without a gate, the same drift recurs the next time a profile-affecting change (a new field, a new
type) ships without a schema re-export.

FIX SHAPE, not prescribed: a check (part of `lore check`, or a new flag/mode) that regenerates each
type's schema in memory and compares it against the committed `.lore/schemas/*.json` bytes,
failing (not merely warning) on a mismatch -- matching this fleet's own stated preference for a
gate over a remembered procedure. Whoever takes this should also decide whether `lore init`/`lore
schema export` should offer to fix the drift it detects, the way other lore commands offer their
own repair path, or whether detection alone (pointing at `lore schema export`) is suffient.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A check exists that detects a committed .lore/schemas/<type>.schema.json whose bytes do not match what schema export would produce from the active profile right now, and fails (non-zero exit) rather than warning only.

The regression case this task found is covered: a profile-visible field addition (e.g. a new relations/claim_* -style property) that changes generated schema bytes without a corresponding lore schema export is caught by the new check, with a test proving it.
A clean, up-to-date bundle (including this repository's own, after the hygiene refresh in this change) passes the new check without modification.
lore instructions and lore help / --help text for the affected command(s) describe the new check and point at lore schema export as the fix.
bun run lint, typecheck and the test suite pass, and lore check exits 0.

A CI job runs lore schema export into a temporary directory and diffs the result against the committed .lore/schemas/, failing on any difference -- asserting drift as a property (export-and-diff against the live generator), never a pinned hash of expected bytes.

The gate is proven in both directions before it ships, as two separate measurements with every other CI job green on both SHAs: a deliberately stale committed schema makes it fail WITH the drift error specifically (not merely red -- a missing lore binary or bad path wears the same colour), and a clean, regenerated tree makes it pass. The lore version/bytes the proof was run against is recorded alongside the result.

implementationNotes:
Scope addition, 2026-09-18, relayed by opum-agent as a Tier-1 operator instruction (the user asked
the question, opum-agent measured the answer, the user told them to send it here) -- taken as scope
without re-confirming, per this fleet's own authority rule.

THE CHECK, now AC#5/#6 above: a CI job that runs `lore schema export` into a temp dir and diffs
against the committed `.lore/schemas/`, failing on any difference. Assert drift as a property
(export-and-diff), never a pinned hash -- a hash only tells a reader which bytes, never whether
they're still current, which is the exact failure this whole thread traces back to.

WHY THIS ISN'T ALREADY COVERED, per opum-agent's own measurement (grepped all five workflow files
across both repos -- ci.yml/promotion-guards.yml here, ci.yml/release.yml/upstream-backlog-watch.yml
on their dev -- for "schema export"/"lore schema"/".lore/schemas"/"drift": zero matches anywhere).
`test/schema-export.test.ts` has ~30 assertions on the EXPORTER (Draft-7 validity, byte-format
contract, --type/--out handling, orphan pruning, etc.) including two that read as if they'd catch
this and don't: "exported bytes are identical to what lore init scaffolds" and "re-exporting
overwrites a stale schema file (regenerates after a profile change)" -- both run entirely inside
temp fixtures/mkdtemp dirs, neither ever reads this repository's own committed `.lore/schemas/`.
That's the object-identity split this fleet keeps naming: the suite measures the EMITTER; the
conclusion a reader draws ("our schemas are right") is about the COMMITTED ARTIFACT. Nothing
bridges them -- which is exactly how the drift from 01f4ef74 (LCLI-477) survived, green CI
throughout, until this thread found it by accident.

PROOF REQUIREMENT (AC#6): both halves of this fleet's own gate-proof convention, as separate
measurements -- deliberately stale schema -> red WITH the drift error (distinguish from a missing
binary or bad path wearing the same red), clean regenerated tree -> green, every other job green on
both SHAs, and the lore version/bytes the proof ran against recorded alongside the result.

Placement (job vs. folding into an existing one), whether it becomes a required context on dev, and
whether it ships with or after LCLI-537/538 are still this task's own implementer's call -- the
sequence agreed earlier (537, 538, 539) is unchanged, only this task's content grew.

Given this becomes CI-gating logic (a candidate required context on dev), get a reviewer pass on
the ci.yml diff specifically before landing, matching this repo's own "a gate that's wrong fails
only during a release" caution even though ci.yml isn't release.yml/scripts/ by name.

SESSION HANDOFF, 2026-09-18, session renewal (fleet orchestrator arranged a restart-pane to pick
up opum-workflow 0.8.6; this session was bound to 0.8.3). No task was In Progress at stop, so this
note carries the summary instead of a per-task status.

WHAT HAPPENED THIS SESSION: opum-agent relayed four items (user-approved) about lore's
type-vocabulary gaps, surfaced while a predecessor session investigated LCLI-534. Each was
independently re-verified against dev at HEAD before acting, not taken on relay:

1. "Promote provenance fields to base fields" -- premise was FALSE as measured. schemaForVersion()
   (src/core/schema.ts) already adds all 7 provenance fields (generated/sources/usage_window/
   verified/status/stale_after/lore_task_status) to EVERY base type, not just Attested Computation
   -- confirmed against every committed .lore/schemas/*.json. No task filed; correction reported
   back to opum-agent. (Separately, opum-agent's OWN repo had a real instance of this for a
   different reason -- their committed schemas were stale, unrelated to lore's design -- tracked as
   their OPAG-198/203, not lore-cli's.)
2. "Validates by construction" -- duplicate of already-filed LCLI-535 (verbatim same ask); a dedupe
   note was added there instead of filing twice.
3. Filed as LCLI-537 ("lore types" command + unknown-type warning naming the valid set). IMPLEMENTED
   AND MERGED: PR #155 (feature), PR #156 (archival move). Reviewed the diff personally before
   merging -- design highlights: field data sourced from the same schemaForVersion() JSON Schema
   `schema export` writes to disk (so a report can never disagree with what's on disk), common-vs-
   type-specific classified by field NAME not by which TOML table declared it, unknown-type warning
   now names the full valid set plus a Levenshtein did-you-mean suggestion. DONE.
4. Filed as LCLI-538 (`strict_types` profile knob). IMPLEMENTED AND MERGED: PR #157, #158 (archival).
   Design decision: a plain boolean `[profile] strict_types = true`, independent of --strict (composes
   with it rather than redefining it). Correctly scoped as implementation-not-design per a two-question
   test opum-agent gave mid-session (does this create/change a contract outside this repo? would
   reversing it need a migration?) -- a plain boolean tripped neither, so it proceeded without
   escalating; a richer enum/list/per-type shape would have needed to go to opum-agent instead. DONE.

DISCOVERED ALONG THE WAY, filed as LCLI-539: lore-cli's OWN committed .lore/schemas/*.json had
drifted from its generator since commit 01f4ef74 (LCLI-477/#76, unnoticed for weeks) -- `lore check`
was clean throughout. Fixed the immediate instance (PR #153, re-exported + verified additive-only:
+4 properties per type, 0 removed, 0 newly-required). LCLI-539 tracks the actual gate so this can't
recur silently -- SCOPE WAS EXPANDED mid-session by a Tier-1 operator instruction (relayed by
opum-agent): must be a CI job that runs `lore schema export` into a temp dir and diffs against
committed `.lore/schemas/`, asserting drift as a property (never a pinned hash), proven BOTH
directions before it ships (deliberate drift -> red WITH the drift error specifically; clean tree ->
green; every other CI job green on both SHAs; record which lore version the proof ran against). Read
LCLI-539's full description + both AC blocks before starting -- there are now 7 ACs, not the original
5. Since this becomes new CI-gating logic (a candidate required context on dev), get a `reviewer` pass
on the ci.yml diff specifically before landing, per this repo's own release/scripts caution extended
to new gates.

LCLI-539 IS NOT STARTED. This is the next task to pick up.

OTHER THINGS WORTH KNOWING:
- Caught and fixed a stale "did-you-mean" comment in src/core/scaffold.ts's DEFAULT_PROFILE_TOML
  that LCLI-537 missed (LCLI-537 fixed profile.ts's docstrings but not this template string); landed
  as a bonus commit inside PR #157.
- Found and reported a quest-cli rough edge (not lore-cli's to fix): `quest task edit --status "Done"`
  set directly (instead of via `task complete`) leaves the record file stranded in tasks/ with no
  direct recovery command -- `task complete` refuses `Done -> Done`. Workaround: demote to an active
  status, then complete properly. quest-cli self-filed this as QCLI-338 before I could file it myself.
- Every write this session (including this one) landed via branch + PR, never a direct push to dev --
  relevant because of a separately-diagnosed fleet mechanism (OFLE-92) where handoff write-mode's
  flush can dirty the committed tracker with no guidance on landing it, and three sessions fleet-wide
  have improvised a direct-to-dev push under recycle pressure. This session's practice avoids that
  independently of the fix landing.
- All branches and worktrees from this session's work are cleaned up; dev was at 99f3e79b (chore
  LCLI-538 archival, #158) before this handoff's own branch.
